caption: The drawing depicts a single object: a lidded, footed serving dish or tureen rendered in pencil on a light-colored background. The tureen has an oval shape with a broad base that narrows slightly upward, resting on a pedestal. The lid fits closely and features a central knob handle. Both the body and the lid are ornamented with raised beadwork along their top and bottom edges. Two symmetrical, ornate handles extend outward from either side of the dish, each with decorative details that suggest twisting or intertwined shapes. Centered on the side of the tureen is a small, finely detailed motif of a reclining animal, likely a lion, which is repeated on both the lid and the body. The entire object is depicted in shades of gray, with careful shading to indicate reflective, metallic surfaces and curved contours. The paper surrounding the drawing is slightly yellowed, and minor brownish marks appear in the upper region outside the object’s boundary. The drawing is framed with a faint rectangular outline, and the name “Hester Duvary” is inscribed in small letters in the bottom left corner.
title: Silver Bowl
